economy.summary: Voted for House Bill 1500 of 2023, which would raise Pennsylvania's minimum wage in stages to $15 per hour; the bill passed the House 103-100 in June 2023.
economy.short: Voted to raise state minimum wage to $15 per hour.

taxes.summary: Sponsored, with Rep. Bob Merski, House Bill 754 of 2025, which would let county retirement boards set supplemental pension increases instead of tying them automatically to the Consumer Price Index; he said the bill balances retirees' purchasing power with protecting counties from unsustainable financial burdens.
taxes.short: Sponsored bill balancing county retiree pension increases with county budgets.

abortion.summary: Voted against Senate Bill 106 of 2022, a proposed package of constitutional amendments that included language stating the Pennsylvania Constitution does not grant any right to abortion or to taxpayer funding of abortion; the measure passed the House 107-92.
abortion.short: Voted against no-constitutional-right-to-abortion amendment package in 2022.

education.summary: Announced, with Rep. Bob Merski, $154,417 in state Competitive Equipment Grants for career and technical education programs in Erie schools, saying that when schools can train students on the same technology used in the workplace, families see clearer pathways to stable careers; this is a funding announcement rather than a broader education platform.
education.short: Announced state grants for Erie career and technical education equipment.

healthcare.summary: Supported Act 77 of 2024, a bipartisan law regulating pharmacy benefit managers by limiting practices such as patient steering and mail-order mandates, saying he was happy it helps independent pharmacies and consumers.
healthcare.short: Supported 2024 law regulating pharmacy benefit manager practices.

energy.summary: Announced a $25,000 state grant for Erie to plan solar panels and a green roof on its municipal building, saying lower utility bills mean more resources for essential services and the project would create local contracting opportunities; this is a funding announcement rather than a broader energy platform.
energy.short: Announced grant for municipal solar planning, citing lower utility bills.

guns.summary: Voted for House Bill 714 of 2023, which would require background checks for private sales and transfers of long guns; the bill passed the House 109-92 in May 2023. He also voted the same day for House Bill 1018, which would create extreme risk protection orders.
guns.short: Voted for expanded background checks and extreme risk protection orders.
